title: Aesthetic Considerations in Architectural Design: Exploring Pleasure, Arousal, and Dominance

findings.antecedent: Architectural elements (form, materiality, color, lighting, spatial organization)
findings.consequent: Well-being, sense of belonging
findings.source: abstract
findings.quote: elements such as form, materiality, color, lighting, and spatial organization, culminating in an atmosphere that nurtures well-being and fosters a sense of belonging

findings.antecedent: Balanced arousal levels in architectural design
findings.consequent: Engagement, active exploration, interaction with the environment
findings.source: abstract
findings.quote: Striking a balance in arousal levels is vital to creating spaces that are engaging without overwhelming occupants, encouraging them to actively explore and interact with the environment.

findings.antecedent: Harmoniously integrated dominant architectural landmarks
findings.consequent: Symbolic identities, city/community character, urban landscape balance
findings.source: abstract
findings.quote: Dominant architectural landmarks often become symbolic identities that shape the character of a city or community.

findings.antecedent: Architectural aesthetics (pleasure, arousal, dominance)
findings.consequent: Human behavior, social interactions, overall well-being
findings.source: abstract
findings.quote: Pleasure, arousal, and dominance are critical psychological factors influencing human behavior, social interactions, and overall well-being.

findings.antecedent: Aesthetically pleasing architectural elements (green spaces, visually appealing facades)
findings.consequent: Positive emotional states
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Joye and van den Berg, 2011)
findings.quote: aesthetically pleasing architectural elements, such as green spaces and visually appealing facades, positively influenced the participants' emotional states.

findings.antecedent: Architectural complexity (overly complex vs. moderately complex)
findings.consequent: Discomfort/dissatisfaction vs. positive emotional experiences
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Nasar and Julian, 1995)
findings.quote: overly complex designs could lead to feelings of discomfort and dissatisfaction, while moderately complex spaces were associated with positive emotional experiences.

findings.antecedent: Beautiful architectural designs
findings.consequent: Activation of brain regions associated with reward and positive emotions (pleasure centers)
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: beautiful architectural designs activated brain regions associated with reward and positive emotions, indicating that aesthetic appeal in architecture has a measurable impact on the brain's pleasure centers.

findings.antecedent: Well-designed healthcare spaces (aesthetically pleasing, calming elements)
findings.consequent: Reduced stress levels, increased patient satisfaction
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Huisman et al., 2012)
findings.quote: well-designed healthcare spaces, featuring aesthetically pleasing and calming elements, contributed to reduced stress levels and increased patient satisfaction.

findings.antecedent: Visually stimulating and harmonious natural environments
findings.consequent: Feelings of relaxation and restoration
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Joye, 2007)
findings.quote: visually stimulating and harmonious natural environments promoted feelings of relaxation and restoration

findings.antecedent: Well-designed public spaces (greenery, comfortable seating, engaging artworks)
findings.consequent: Positive emotions, sense of pleasure among visitors
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Joye and De Block, 2011)
findings.quote: well-designed public spaces, featuring aesthetically pleasing elements such as greenery, comfortable seating, and engaging artworks, elicited positive emotions and a sense of pleasure among visitors.

findings.antecedent: Interior design (warm color palettes, soft textures, personalized decor)
findings.consequent: Higher sense of pleasure, comfort, attachment to the home
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Horelli et al., 2016)
findings.quote: use of warm color palettes, soft textures, and personalized decor contributed to a higher sense of pleasure, comfort, and attachment to the home.

findings.antecedent: Well-designed educational spaces (natural light, vibrant colors, interactive learning areas)
findings.consequent: Students' engagement, pleasure in the learning process

findings.consequent: Pleasurable experiences, positive emotions, increased user satisfaction, attachment
findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Mugge and Schifferstein, 2004)

findings.antecedent: Design features (natural elements); Cultural differences

findings.source: Review of Related Literature (Vartanian et al., 2019)
findings.quote: while some design features, such as natural elements, tended to evoke pleasure across cultures, cultural differences influenced preferences for specific aesthetic elements.

findings.antecedent: Architectural complexity (moderately complex exhibits)

minimum_safe_summary: This narrative review, 'Aesthetic Considerations in Architectural Design: Exploring Pleasure, Arousal, and Dominance,' synthesizes existing literature to understand how architectural aesthetics influence human emotions, behavior, and well-being. The core claim is that thoughtful integration of pleasure, arousal, and dominance in architectural design can create transformative spaces that inspire and resonate with individuals. Key findings indicate that balanced complexity, harmonious proportions, appropriate color schemes, varied textures, and thoughtful lighting contribute to pleasure and comfort. Arousal is influenced by dynamic elements, spatial composition, movement, patterns, and contrasts, while dominance is conveyed through scale, materials, form, and geometry, contributing to urban identity and orientation. The review highlights that aesthetically pleasing environments, especially those incorporating natural elements, reduce stress, improve concentration, and enhance overall satisfaction. The paper does not explicitly state its own limitations as a review.
